name: New Federal Alcohol Permits Weekly
pitch: Every new federal basic permit for wineries, distilleries, alcohol importers and wholesalers each week, for label printers, packaging and bottling suppliers who want to reach a new producer before it picks vendors

provenAbroad.what: UK: lists of newly formed companies sold to service firms by subscription (Companies House directory about 30 GBP a month, cheaper digest software), the same new-entity model on a different register
US: a TTB permittee scraper is sold per result to spirits brokers, glass and closure vendors, label printers and bottling-line makers

buyer.who: Label printers and packaging suppliers that serve wineries and distilleries
buyer.countNote: IBISWorld: 1,465 Packaging and Labeling Services businesses in 2026; label printers inside general printing are not counted
buyer.reach: Suppliers publish a business inbox on their own websites; the buyer trades are named by an existing reseller of this data

price.reason: Lowest band price; no competitor with a public monthly price was found, and the weekly volume is thin

data.publisher: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB), US Treasury
data.dataset: Basic Permits Issued Since the Last Publication (FOIA frequently requested list, CSV)
data.subject: a newly permitted alcohol business (permit number, owner and operating name, premises address, industry type)
data.recordsNote: Not counted per month: the file holds only the latest weekly publication. The Oct 19, 2026 file has 78 rows (25 importers, 26 wholesalers, 12 distilled spirits plants, 15 wine producers), all with a business suffix on the owner name. A monthly count needs four weekly snapshots. Breweries are not published (IRC 6103).
data.privacy: All 78 owner names in the Oct 19 file carry a business suffix; keep that filter so a permit held by a named person never ships.

license.note: TTB says TTB.gov is a public domain website and anyone may download its information at no cost without special permission.

risks: Thin: about 78 new permits a week nationally, and importers and wholesalers are weaker leads for label printers than producers. No paying competitor proves a monthly price.
